text:
I've now read the entire codebase — all 14 source modules, the 5 test files, config, packaging, and the precomputed outputs. Here's my honest assessment.

## Overall

This is a **well-engineered research replication**, not a rough draft. It's unusually disciplined for something that "nobody has audited": the math is factored into pure, unit-tested numpy functions (`vectors.py`, `elo.py`); the model wrapper isolates the genuinely tricky parts (capture/steering hooks) and tests them against a tiny randomly-initialized Gemma-2 plus a real-model integration test; the README documents every deviation from the paper and the layer/token conventions; seeds are set; outputs are reproducible (the committed `manifest.json` matches the code paths). The hard, easy-to-get-wrong details are mostly *right*: BOS exclusion from PCA, mean-centering scenario probes against the shared template, span-overlap token masking (boundary-correct and tested), gauge-fixing the Bradley–Terry fit, both A/B orderings to cancel position bias, `attn_implementation="eager"` (recommended for Gemma-2's soft-capping).

The issues I found are minor — latent/portability bugs and a few silent-failure edge cases, not correctness defects in the core method.

## Concrete issues

| # | File:line | Sev | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `pyproject.toml:13`, `requirements.txt:2` (used at `model.py:56-59`) | med | `from_pretrained(dtype=...)` requires a recent transformers; the declared floor `>=4.42` only accepted `torch_dtype`, so a minimum-version install silently ignores `dtype` and loads fp32 (3× slower, different numerics). Bump the floor or use `torch_dtype`. |
| 2 | `stories.py:136` | med | `urllib.request.urlopen(req)` has no `timeout=`; a hung endpoint blocks dataset generation forever. Also the `api_base` scheme is unvalidated (env-controlled `file://` would read local files). |
| 3 | `model.py:191-193` | low | `span_mean_activations`: a span that matches zero tokens gives `denominator.clamp(min=1)` → a silently all-zero activation row that quietly corrupts the Elo correlation instead of raising. |
| 4 | `vectors.py:66` | low | `pca_components`: the explained-variance ratio denominator is all eigenvalues in the `d<=n` branch but only the kept positive ones in the `d>n` branch, so the variance-target cutoff `k` is computed against slightly different totals depending on which path runs (per-layer, see manifest). |
| 5 | `steer.py:108-109` | low | Steered-emotion selection (`order[::-1][:k-k//2] + order[:k//2]`) has no dedup/bounds guard; if `n_steered_emotions` approaches the emotion count the top and bottom slices can overlap and steer the same emotion twice. |
| 6 | `validate.py:123`, `steer.py:183` | low | `_write_csv` is duplicated verbatim across two modules — should live in one helper. |
| 7 | `config.yaml:5` | nit | Comment claims bf16 is "~3× faster than fp32" on CPU; that only holds on AMX hardware and is misleading as a general default for CPU runs. |

None of these is a blocking correctness bug. Nothing touches the validity of the extracted vectors or the steering result.

## Lines to rewrite

Small — roughly **20 lines**: the dtype/version fix (~2), an HTTP timeout (~1), a zero-span guard (~3), the PCA ratio consistency fix (~2), a dedup guard on steered emotions (~2), and folding the duplicated CSV writer into a shared util (~10 net).

## Bottom line

**Yes — I'd approve this.** It's solid, tested, and honest about its own scope. The findings above are non-blocking nits I'd leave as review comments (fix #1 and #2 before any real GPU run, since a too-old transformers and a hangable HTTP call are the only ones that bite in practice). This is in good shape to bring back into active development.
